questionsToConsider: Are all four results equally nice to get? A shareable quiz works when nobody feels embarrassed by their outcome.
Does each scenario have one answer for every friend type, so the scoring stays fair?
Will you post this on social media, send it in a newsletter or run it at an event?
guide.howToUseResponses: Check the split across the four results after the first day. If one friend type rarely comes up, one of its answers in each question is probably less appealing than the others, so reword it. If you run the quiz for a brand, the most common result is a friendly hook for your next post.
customizeSteps: Pick your own four types, then rewrite each scenario so every option matches one type, scored from zero to three in the same order.
Keep the bands spaced evenly if you add questions, and test each result by answering with one type all the way through.
Share the link where your audience already talks, and invite people to send it on to the friend they named.

faqs.a: A clear theme, quick questions and a result people are happy to show off. Every outcome should feel like a compliment.

faqs.q: How does this quiz choose a friend type?
faqs.a: Each answer is worth zero to three points on a scale from calm to spontaneous. The total falls into one of four bands, and each band has its own result.

faqs.q: Can I change the friend types?
faqs.a: Yes. Rename the four results and rewrite the answers so each one still points to a single type, then test each result.

doc.title: What kind of friend are you?
doc.description: Five group-chat scenarios that sort people into one of four friend types.

blocks.title: Every friend group has a listener, a planner, a hype person and an adventurer. Five scenarios and we'll tell you which one you are.
What's your role in the group chat?

options.label: I reply properly when someone needs to talk
I'm the one setting a date and a place
I send voice notes and far too many reactions
I'm offline, but I show up with a story later

blocks.title: A friend's birthday is coming up. You...

options.label: Write a card that makes them cry a little
Book the table and remind everyone twice
Plan a surprise and make sure it's loud
Take them somewhere they've never been

blocks.title: Friday plans fall through at the last minute. What happens?

options.label: I check the person who cancelled is OK
I have a backup plan ready in five minutes
I rally everyone else to come to mine
Perfect excuse for something spontaneous

blocks.title: Your friends are planning a trip together. Your job is...

options.label: Making sure the quieter ones get a say
The spreadsheet, the budget and the bookings
The playlist and the group photos
Finding the thing nobody else would try

blocks.title: A friend texts you some bad news. Your first move is to...

options.label: Call them and mostly listen
Work out what practical help they need
Tell them how brilliant they are until they believe it
Get them out of the house for a change of scene

blocks.title: Who's the first friend you'd send this quiz to?
blocks.description: Just for fun. We won't contact them.

endings.title: You're the listener 💛
endings.bodyMd: You're the friend people call first when something goes wrong. You notice who's gone quiet and you make room for them.

endings.title: You're the adventurer 🧭
endings.bodyMd: You're the reason your friends have stories to tell. When things get routine, you're the one who says yes to something new.

endings.title: You're the hype person 🎉
endings.bodyMd: You bring the energy. Your friends feel celebrated around you, and every good moment gets louder when you're there.

endings.title: You're the planner 🗓️
endings.bodyMd: Without you, the group chat would still be saying "we should do something". You turn ideas into dates, and your friends quietly rely on it.
